newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - LIG says recovery phase over.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - LIG says recovery phase over.

text.p: Resurgent British-based condom and rubber glove maker London International Group Plc (LIG) said on Thursday that its three-year recovery phase was now over, and that it was poised to enter a new stage of growth.

In a telephone interview with Reuters, chief executive Nick Hodges said LIG planned to grow both organically and through further acquisitions in each of its core areas and promised "double-digit earnings growth for the next few years."
"That is a sign of how confident we are," he added.

The company has succeeded in turning itself around since it chalked up a 175 million stg loss in the year ended March 1994, achieving its target of returning to pre-crash levels of profitability by the middle of 1997.
"We are saying that this is the end of the recovery - we are back to where we should have been," Hodges said.
After net exceptional charges of 6.1 million stg, pre-tax profits rose 12.6 percent to 29.5 million stg.

Profit margins also continued to progress towards the group's 15 percent target, improving to 12.3 percent from 10.1 percent a year earlier. Hodges said that if newer businesses were excluded, margins stood at 13.1 percent, and added that the group was on track to achieve the 15 percent goal in the current year.
Hodges said markets for the group's core products, which include the Durex condom brand and gloves for medical, household and industrial use, "are not mature."
"We believe that all the core businesses in surgical gloves, condoms and industrial gloves still have a long way to go in terms of market share, new products and finding new users," he said.
Hodges said the group's marketing spend, which goes mainly on its condom brands, would rise by 20 percent in the current year to around 36 million stg.

The company also announced its intention to roll out the Avanti polyurethane condom, the world's only non-latex condom which LIG says offers allergy and sensitivity advantages, world-wide. Hodges said this was a good example of the way the group would be moving forward.

LIG will also continue on the acquisition trail, adding to the U.S. Aladan glove and condom business, Portuguese glove maker Franco and Spanish condom brand Androtex bought in the last financial year.
"We are in a very strong cash position," said Hodges, with net operating cash flow in the year rising to 37.6 million stg from 34.0 million.
The strong pound cut the group's pre-tax profit by 1.4 million stg in the year to March 31, and Hodges said it could adversely affect current-year earnings but declined to give details.
